newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Opus to get controlling black shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Opus to get controlling black shareholders.

text.p: South African gambling group, Opus Investments Ltd, on Wednesday announced a deal which will see black empowerment groups, including Moribo Investments Ltd, becoming its controlling shareholders in the future.
It said the new shareholders will allow Opus to take advantage of opportunities in provincial video gaming and the national lottery which are expected to arise from June 1997 onwards.

Opus said agreement had been reached in principle whereby it will initially acquire certain of the leisure and sporting assets of Moribo, a wholly-owned subsidiary of major South African black group Thebe Investment Corp.
Moribo already owns a 13.2 percent stake in Opus.
At the same time, Opus' controlling shareholders will renounce their rights in future rights issues, at which time Moribo will increase its holding in Opus.
Opus said talks were currently taking place with other empowerment groups which will be entitled to take up shares in the firm.

"The expected future shareholders of the economic empowerment groups, including Moribo, will constitute a majority control of Opus issued ordinary share capital and the future rights issues...," the group said.
Shareholders were advised to continue exercising caution in their sharedealings until a further announcement was made.
